analysis:
The PR changes only docs/developer/build.md; it is documentation with no executable code. I examined both the base excerpt (lines 935-1246) and the head excerpt (lines 1-443). The head excerpt is only a partial view of the new file and does not reach the end, so the later part of the head file was not reviewed.

Security-relevant statements in the visible text:
- The release flow (head 257-263) says signing, R2 staging and publication run as separate jobs. The scoped POST /v1/releases registers the exact official build. Retries reuse the original signed artifact. Secret-bearing jobs accept only verified signed production tags in reviewed master ancestry. This is consistent with A-005, A-011, A-017, T-024 and T-054.
- The docs say CI establishes official identity, not runtime Apple success, and that no per-release hardware qualification is required. This matches the TB-011 header comments in the canonical context.
- Native qualification is described as default-off and refusing without opt-in. This is consistent with the T-052 posture.
- CI statements (cache restore/discard, content-verified timestamps, no signing keys in caches) are descriptive. They cannot be checked against the workflows, because the workflow files are not in this batch.

I found no invalidated threat assumption and no new attack surface. For the next pass: the workflow, script and release-publication files that these docs describe are not in this batch, and I did not verify those claims against them.
